entities.summary: Johann Eduard Erdmann was a German Lutheran pastor, historian of philosophy, and philosopher of religion, of which he wrote on the mediation of faith and knowledge. He was known to be a follower of Friedrich Schleiermacher, whom he studied under August Carlblom, and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, whom he regarded as his mentor. Erdmann also studied the works of Karl Daub. Historians of philosophy usually include Erdmann as a member of the Right Wing of the Hegelian movement, a group of thinkers who were also referred to variously as the Right Hegelians (Rechtshegelianer), the Hegelian Right, and/or as the Old Hegelians (Althegelianer).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Erdmann's philosophical works on faith and knowledge influenced the development of German theology in the 19th century, particularly among the Right Hegelian movement. His ideas continue to be studied by historians of philosophy today.
